why_now: Refine (Mudit): explore the more commonly heard bhajans 'Haare Ka Tu Hai Sahara' and 'Dinanath Meri Baat' alongside 'Sheesh Ke Daani'.

Result — 'Haare Ka Tu Hai Sahara Saware': a modern, credited song, not traditional. JioSaavn credits Kanhiya Mittal (singer/composer/lyricist), label Kanhiya Mittal Entertainments, released 18 Feb 2022, ~794K plays; lyric sites note the last stanza carries the writer's chhap 'Sanju'. A cover = label-owned song → fails the copyright hard filter (AVOID as a cover).

Result — 'Dinanath Meri Baat Chhani Koni Tere Se': sources disagree. hindibhajan.in lists the lyrics as 'Traditional' (Lakhbir Singh Lakha, Lakhdatar Music); JioSaavn credits Sanju Sharma as lyricist/composer (Saawariya Music And Films, 25 May 2023, ~150K plays). BhaktiBharat shows no author chhap. Rights unclear → NEEDS CHECK; do not cover until a folk/traditional origin is confirmed or a licence is obtained — and even then, don't copy any label's tune/arrangement (Content ID matches melody).

Best way to capture that demand legally: 'Haare Ka Sahara' and 'Dinanath' are traditional epithets of Shyam Baba, not owned phrases. Build our ORIGINAL bhajan's chorus and title around 'Haare Ka Sahara' (the most-heard phrase) with 'Sheesh Ke Daani' and 'Dinanath' in the verses — one song rides all three search phrases.

Story hook (verified as tradition): Barbarika vowed to fight for whichever side was losing — hence 'Haare Ka Sahara', the support of those who have lost. A 45-sec Short 'Why is Shyam Baba called Haare Ka Sahara?' is a strong, zero-copyright explainer.
Shorts demand for 'Sheesh ke Daani' still hot: 'Respect zone 111+' Shorts at 1.73M (≈10h), 1.36M and 1.19M views (24–25 Sep) in our collector data.
YouTube autocomplete today: 'khatu shyam bhajan' → 'new', 'new 2025', 'remix', 'nonstop', 'aarti', 'happy birthday' — searchers want NEW bhajans and Janmotsav songs, so an original has room.

Key dates: next Gyaras (Papankusha Ekadashi) 21/22 Oct (confirm local panchang) — pilot Short; Shyam Janmotsav = Dev Uthani Ekadashi, Fri 20 Nov 2026 — T-14 brief 6 Nov, publish window 13–19 Nov, T-5 hard deadline 15 Nov.

Optional (not zero-budget): if Mudit really wants a cover of 'Haare Ka Tu Hai Sahara', ask Kanhiya Mittal Entertainments for written permission / a cover licence first; otherwise the video will be claimed or struck.

I want to explore those as well.
